Meanwhile every busy database faces the same bottleneck: disk reads cost far more than memory reads. A cache sits between the query layer and storage, holding hot rows so repeated lookups return in microseconds rather than grinding through spinning platters.

However a cache introduces the hardest problem in computing: knowing when stored data has gone stale. Teams pick expiry windows, or they invalidate keys directly on write; both paths leak edge cases. Read through designs hide this from callers, while write behind designs risk losing updates if the cache node dies suddenly under heavy load.

Along with that capacity limits push out old data. LRU drops what nobody wants; random policy costs almost nothing to run. Sharding across many hosts adds room, but a hot key can still pin all traffic onto a solitary box, stalling many fast lookups.

Finally measure your cache hit ratio, watch evictions, and tune sizes; a well tuned cache leaves most heavy work done.
